title: The New Hope, and New Worry, of Kamala Harris

sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Vice President Kamala Harris riding a wave of Democratic Party endorsements taking her place as the frontrunner for the nomination.
sentences.zh: 副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯乘着民主党背书的浪潮，确立了她作为总统候选人提名领跑者的地位。

sentences.en: Bill and Hillary Clinton writing, now is the time to support Kamala Harris and fight with everything we've got to elect her.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿和希拉里·克林顿写道，现在是支持卡玛拉·哈里斯并竭尽全力推选她的时候了。

sentences.en: As Democrat after Democrat, races to annoy Kamala Harris as President Biden's replacement.
sentences.zh: 随着一位又一位民主党人竞相拥护卡玛拉·哈里斯接替拜登总统。

sentences.en: There are now six Democratic governors who have endorsed Kamala Harris' presidential bid.
sentences.zh: 目前已有六位民主党州长支持卡玛拉·哈里斯竞选总统。

sentences.en: California Governor Gavin Newsom, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽森，宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗。

sentences.en: Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi is out with a full-throated endorsement of Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 前众议院议长南希·佩洛西发表了对卡玛拉·哈里斯的全力支持。

sentences.en: The governor of Maine.
sentences.zh: 缅因州州长。

sentences.en: And now the latest is New York Governor Kathy Hochul.
sentences.zh: 最新的一位是纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔。

sentences.en: It's become clear that, much like Biden himself,
sentences.zh: 显而易见，就像拜登本人一样，

sentences.en: Harris will face no real competition in her path to the Democratic nomination, despite polling that shows weaknesses in her candidacy.
sentences.zh: 尽管民调显示她的候选资格存在弱点，但哈里斯在通往民主党提名的道路上不会面临真正的竞争。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues Nate Cohn and Reid Epstein about why that is and what it may mean for her campaign.
sentences.zh: 我和同事内特·科恩以及里德·爱泼斯坦讨论了原因，以及这对她的竞选意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, July 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月23日，星期二。

sentences.en: Nate, I just want to begin by welcoming you back from paternity leave, as they say, out of the frying pan and into the fire.
sentences.zh: 内特，我想先欢迎你结束陪产假归来，正如人们所说，刚出火坑又入火海。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So, as we speak with you, Nate, the Democratic Party is in the process of putting almost all of its political support
sentences.zh: 内特，就在我们和你交谈时，民主党正在将其几乎所有的政治支持

sentences.en: and its financial muscle behind Kamala Harris as the nominee to replace Joe Biden, led by Biden himself, who endorsed her.
sentences.zh: 以及财力投入到卡玛拉·哈里斯身上，让她接替乔·拜登成为候选人，这由拜登本人带头支持。

sentences.en: And the collective message that this has been sending is that Democrats, especially the party brass,
sentences.zh: 而这所传递出的集体信息是，民主党人，尤其是党内高层，

sentences.en: believe Harris can win, that she has a better chance than Biden of defeating Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 相信哈里斯能赢，相信她比拜登更有机会击败唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And so we want to fact-check that with you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想和你核实一下这一点。

sentences.en: Is Kamala Harris a strong nominee in the race against Donald Trump and is coronating her, as the party seems to be doing, a wise decision based on the numbers?
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯在与唐纳德·特朗普的竞选中是一位强有力的候选人吗？党内似乎正在进行的加冕仪式，从数据上看是一个明智的决定吗？

sentences.en: Well, you laid out three facts for me to check.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你列出了三个事实让我核实。

sentences.en: And I think that two of them check out.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中两个是成立的。

sentences.en: One thing that checks out is that Kamala Harris enters the race as a stronger candidate than Joe Biden was as he exits.
sentences.zh: 有一点是成立的，那就是卡玛拉·哈里斯作为候选人进入竞选时，比乔·拜登退出时要强。

sentences.en: His favorability ratings and approval ratings were in the 30s.
sentences.zh: 他的好感度和支持率都在30%左右。

sentences.en: He trailed Donald Trump by a wide margin in the national and state polls.
sentences.zh: 他在全国和各州民调中都大幅落后于唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris in the early polling looks a little stronger than that.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯在早期民调中看起来比那要强一些。

sentences.en: The second thing that checks out is that Kamala Harris can win.
sentences.zh: 第二点成立的是，卡玛拉·哈里斯能够获胜。

sentences.en: She starts out a little bit behind in the polls, but not by a lot.
sentences.zh: 她在民调中起步稍稍落后，但差距不大。

sentences.en: And frankly, there's a whole campaign ahead of her.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，她面前还有整个竞选过程。

sentences.en: It's not clear that we should read a ton into her initial standing.
sentences.zh: 我们不应过度解读她最初的民调表现。

sentences.en: She'll have every opportunity to improve and persuade the public that she should be her party's nominee.
sentences.zh: 她将有充分的机会去提升自己，并说服公众她应该成为党内候选人。

sentences.en: The third thing you said, though, is that Kamala Harris is a strong nominee.
sentences.zh: 不过，你说的第三点是，卡玛拉·哈里斯是一位强有力的候选人。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that is as easy to defend.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这一点是否容易站得住脚。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Walk us through why that's not a defensible claim.
sentences.zh: 请为我们分析一下为什么这个说法站不住脚。

sentences.en: I think the simplest way to demonstrate that is just to look at her favorability ratings.
sentences.zh: 我认为最简单的证明方法就是看看她的好感度评分。

sentences.en: And that's a jargony term for whether Americans say they like Kamala Harris or not.
sentences.zh: 这是一个专业术语，指美国人是否表示他们喜欢卡玛拉·哈里斯。

sentences.en: And for years, pollsters have found that a majority of Americans do not have a favorable view of Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 多年来，民调机构发现大多数美国人对卡玛拉·哈里斯并没有好感。

sentences.en: Other way you can look at it is in terms of the race against Trump.
sentences.zh: 另一种看待方式是看她与特朗普的竞选情况。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris may be running a little bit better than Joe Biden, but Kamala Harris has trailed Donald Trump in almost every national and battleground state poll this cycle.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯的表现可能比乔·拜登好一点，但在这个周期里，她在几乎所有的全国和摇摆州民调中都落后于唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I want to make sure everyone absorbs that.
sentences.zh: 我想确保每个人都消化了这个信息。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris has trailed the man that she is now being set up to run against in this general election
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯在这次大选中落后于她现在被安排去对抗的那个人，

sentences.en: in almost every national and battleground state poll that you have seen this year.
sentences.zh: 在今年你所看到的几乎所有全国和摇摆州民调中都是如此。

sentences.en: That is correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And, you know, we should put the big caveat out there, which is that Kamala Harris has not been a candidate for president in any of those polls.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们应该提出一个重要的前提，那就是在所有这些民调中，卡玛拉·哈里斯并不是总统候选人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: People have been asked to contemplate her as that thing in those polls, but she wasn't that thing.
sentences.zh: 人们在那些民调中被要求考虑她作为候选人的情况，但她当时并不是候选人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: We're asking voters to consider her hypothetical.
sentences.zh: 我们是在让选民考虑她的假设情况。

sentences.en: And Kamala Harris is a well-known candidate.
sentences.zh: 而且卡玛拉·哈里斯是一位广为人知的候选人。

sentences.en: You know, she's run for president before.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她以前竞选过总统。

sentences.en: She's the vice president.
sentences.zh: 她是副总统。

sentences.en: Voters aren't coming to this question with no information about her at all.
sentences.zh: 选民在面对这个问题时并非对她一无所知。

sentences.en: So I think that it's reasonable to read something into the polling we've seen to this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，解读我们目前看到的民调结果是合理的。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, it's worth noting she's going to reintroduce herself to the public, and maybe she'll come out of that stronger.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，值得注意的是，她将重新向公众介绍自己，也许她会因此变得更强。

sentences.en: She might also come out of it weaker.
sentences.zh: 她也可能因此变得更弱。

sentences.en: Republicans will attack her, and voters haven't heard that either.
sentences.zh: 共和党人会攻击她，而选民也还没听过那些攻击。

sentences.en: But the point is that as she enters the race, she does so behind and without a tremendous amount
sentences.zh: 但重点是，当她进入竞选时，她处于落后状态，而且没有获得

sentences.en: of goodwill from the voters in the middle of the electorate who will likely decide the election.
sentences.zh: 可能决定选举结果的中间选民的大量好感。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: In the most recent Times-Siena poll of Pennsylvania, which is probably the single most important state in this election.
sentences.zh: 在最近一次《纽约时报》与锡耶纳学院对宾夕法尼亚州的民调中，这可能是这次选举中最重要的一个州。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The swingiest of the swing states in this election.
sentences.zh: 这是这次选举中最摇摆的摇摆州。

sentences.en: But only 42% of likely voters said they had a favorable impression of Kamala Harris, and 55% said unfavorable.
sentences.zh: 但只有42%的可能选民表示对卡玛拉·哈里斯有好感，而55%的人表示反感。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That makes her less popular than Donald Trump, who had a 46% favorability rating in our poll.
sentences.zh: 这使她比唐纳德·特朗普更不受欢迎，他在我们的民调中好感度为46%。

sentences.en: And it makes her a lot less popular than Joe Biden was four years ago when he won the state with a 51% favorability rating.
sentences.zh: 而且这使她比四年前乔·拜登以51%的好感度赢得该州时要不受欢迎得多。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And he only won narrowly, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，他当时也只是险胜。

sentences.en: And how do we need a count for that?
sentences.zh: 我们需要如何解释这一点呢？

sentences.en: Why Harris is trailing Trump so consistently and struggling in a make-or-break swing state like Pennsylvania?
sentences.zh: 为什么哈里斯如此持续地落后于特朗普，并在宾夕法尼亚州这样关键的摇摆州苦苦挣扎？

sentences.en: How do you understand that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么理解的？

sentences.en: One way to think about it is to think about how Democrats have handled every election really since 2016.
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是回顾民主党自2016年以来的历次选举表现。

sentences.en: Beginning as soon as the 2018 midterm elections, Democrats committed to nominating relatively
sentences.zh: 从2018年中期选举开始，民主党就致力于提名相对

sentences.en: moderate, well-liked, broadly acceptable candidates who had the potential to appeal to almost any voter who didn't like Donald Trump or his, you know, MAGA allies.
sentences.zh: 温和、受欢迎、被广泛接受的候选人，他们有潜力吸引任何不喜欢唐纳德·特朗普或他的“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）盟友的选民。

sentences.en: You know, in the 2018 midterms, they nominated political newcomers who were military veterans who were blank slates on the issues and were moderates.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在2018年中期选举中，他们提名了政治新人，他们是退伍军人，在议题上是一张白纸，而且是温和派。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We spoke to a lot of them on The Daily in that period.
sentences.zh: 我们在那段时期的《每日新闻》中采访过很多这样的人。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about Alyssa Slocken in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是密歇根州的艾丽莎·斯洛特金。

sentences.en: Great example.
sentences.zh: 很好的例子。

sentences.en: Mikey Sherrill, Abby Spanberger, Jason Crowe.
sentences.zh: 米基·谢里尔、阿比·斯潘伯格、杰森·克罗。

sentences.en: I mean, we can go on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还可以列举更多。

sentences.en: In almost every district, it felt like the Democrats plucked someone who Republicans just weren't going to have much to say againSt.
sentences.zh: 在几乎每个选区，感觉民主党都挑选了一个共和党人无法对其进行太多攻击的人。

sentences.en: And that made it a pretty simple election in these districts, right?
sentences.zh: 这使得这些选区的选举变得相当简单，对吧？

sentences.en: Voters knew they didn't like Trump and the Republicans, and the Democrats put forward someone with a smile.
sentences.zh: 选民知道他们不喜欢特朗普和共和党人，而民主党人推举了一个面带微笑的人选。

sentences.en: They didn't necessarily have enthusiastic bases of support, but they were acceptable to an electorate that did not want to support Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他们未必有热情的支持基础，但对于不想支持共和党人的选民群体来说，他们是可以接受的。

sentences.en: We saw the same thing in 2020 with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我们在2020年的乔·拜登身上也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is a perfect example of someone who wasn't exactly loved by the Democratic base, but was he acceptable to a Republican moderate in the suburbs?
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登是一个完美的例子，他并不完全受民主党基础选民的喜爱，但他对于郊区的共和党温和派来说是可以接受的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he was a relatively moderate elder statesman.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是一位相对温和的政坛元老。

sentences.en: And they did it again in the midterms in 2022, where they ran well-liked incumbents.
sentences.zh: 他们在2022年的中期选举中又做了一次，当时他们推举了受欢迎的在任者。

sentences.en: Mark Kelly in Arizona, Raphael Warnock, Gretchen Whitmer, Josh Shapiro.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州的马克·凯利、拉斐尔·沃诺克、格雷琴·惠特默、乔什·夏皮罗。

sentences.en: These are broadly appealing candidates who didn't come with a lot of baggage and made it easy for voters who didn't want to vote for Republicans, who didn't want to vote for MAGA,
sentences.zh: 这些都是具有广泛吸引力的候选人，他们没有太多的政治包袱，这使得那些不想投票给共和党人、不想投票给MAGA的选民，

sentences.en: to vote against MAGA, and to vote against Republicans, because there wasn't much that Republicans could put forward to argue against those Democrats.
sentences.zh: 能够投票反对MAGA，投票反对共和党人，因为共和党人拿不出太多理由来反驳这些民主党人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, Nate, how much of Harris's problem, based on the data you cited a few moments ago, can be traced to her falling outside of that broadly acceptable moderate archetype
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，根据你刚才引用的数据，哈里斯的问题在多大程度上可以归结为她不符合那种广泛可接受的温和派原型，

sentences.en: that you just described that has defined the post-2016 Democratic playbook?
sentences.zh: 也就是你刚才描述的定义了2016年后民主党竞选策略的那种原型？

sentences.en: And if so, why doesn't she fit in to that mold?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，为什么她不符合那种模式？

sentences.en: I don't think she fits neatly into that mold.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她能完全契合那种模式。

sentences.en: And she brings a bit of baggage to the election that might make it challenging for her to put herself back in to that bucket.
sentences.zh: 而且她带有一些政治包袱，这可能使她难以将自己重新归入那一类。

sentences.en: Going all the way back to the beginning of her political career, this is someone who rose in politics in the San Francisco Bay Area, one of the most liberal places in the country.
sentences.zh: 追溯到她政治生涯的起点，她是在旧金山湾区崛起的，那是全国最自由派的地方之一。

sentences.en: And to win politically there, she had to win among Democrats and among liberal Democrats.
sentences.zh: 为了在那里赢得政治胜利，她必须在民主党人和自由派民主党人中获胜。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily something that sets her up to be popular among swing voters nationwide.
sentences.zh: 这未必能让她在全国范围内的摇摆选民中受欢迎。

sentences.en: To become a U.S.
sentences.zh: 为了成为美国参议员，

sentences.en: Senator, she didn't necessarily even have to beat a Republican.
sentences.zh: 她甚至未必需要击败共和党人。

sentences.en: She did have to beat a Republican to become Attorney General in 2010 and to win re-election in 2014.
sentences.zh: 她在2010年竞选总检察长和2014年竞选连任时确实需要击败共和党人。

sentences.en: But the critical political challenge that Kamala Harris built her career around was overcoming the opposition of other Democrats in one of the bluest states in the country.
sentences.zh: 但卡玛拉·哈里斯职业生涯所围绕的关键政治挑战，是在全国最蓝的州之一克服其他民主党人的反对。

sentences.en: When she ran for president in 2019, I think it revealed that that experience brought with her a series of political instincts that didn't necessarily map neatly onto the demands of
sentences.zh: 当她在2019年竞选总统时，我认为这表明那种经历带给她的一系列政治直觉，并不一定能与全国政治的需求完全吻合。

sentences.en: national politics.
sentences.zh: 她在“全民医保”、是否禁止水力压裂法以及其他问题上向左翼靠拢，

sentences.en: She ran to the left on Medicare for All, on whether she would ban fracking, and on other
sentences.zh: 这些问题使她难以看起来像那种广泛可接受的候选人，

sentences.en: issues that made it challenging for her to look like the kind of broadly acceptable candidate
sentences.zh: 这会给共和党人在大选过程中提供许多攻击她的机会。

sentences.en: will give Republicans many opportunities to attack her in the course of the general election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们已经在这么做了。

sentences.en: In fact, they're already doing that.
sentences.zh: 特朗普和他的盟友已经称卡玛拉·哈里斯为左翼人物。

sentences.en: Trump and his allies are already calling Kamala Harris a left-wing figure.
sentences.zh: 根据你所说的一切，她很容易受到这种攻击和这种认知的影响。

sentences.en: And based on everything you're saying, she is vulnerable to that line of attack and to that perception.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，总的来说，她的竞选活动并不总是以出色的政治运作而著称。

sentences.en: And, you know, in general, her campaigns have not always been characterized by, you know, tremendous political acting.
sentences.zh: 她2019年的竞选确实很挣扎，她在艾奥瓦州初选前很久就退出了。

sentences.en: Her 2019 campaign really struggled, and she was out of the race long before Iowa.
sentences.zh: 她的竞选活动被广泛认为管理不善。

sentences.en: Her campaign was widely viewed as mismanaged.
sentences.zh: 她在竞选中难以找到一个真实的政治信息，她似乎一直在追逐选民，追逐那些似乎在向左转的民主党人，所以她跟随他们去了那里。

sentences.en: She struggled to find an authentic political message in that campaign, and she sort of seemed
sentences.zh: 但她在这一点上也不是特别真实。

sentences.en: to be chasing the electorate, chasing the Democrats who seemed to be moving to the left, and so she followed them there.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她可能处于一种需要在大选中尝试追回选民的境地。

sentences.en: But she wasn't really especially authentic at that either.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And now she may be in the position where she needs to try and chase the electorate pack the other way in the general election.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们在2019年卡玛拉·哈里斯竞选民主党提名期间做过一期节目，标题就是《卡玛拉·哈里斯代表什么？》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 那是在我们的同事亚历克斯·伯恩斯采访了时任参议员哈里斯之后，

sentences.en: I remember an episode we did during this period when Kamala Harris was running for the Democratic nomination in 2019 that was literally entitled, What Does Kamala Harris Stand For?
sentences.zh: 在采访中，他与她谈到了在那段时期给她的意识形态贴上任何标签是多么困难。

sentences.en: And it came on the back of an interview that our colleague Alex Burns did with then-Senator
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Harris in which he talked to her about how hard it was to put any kind of an ideological label on her in that period.
sentences.zh: 而且她担任副总统的任期也未必有什么突出的表现。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统在执政初期让她负责处理边境问题。

sentences.en: And her tenure as vice president hasn't necessarily been marked with distinction either.
sentences.zh: 边境问题现在是民主党在这次选举中面临的最大政治负担之一。

sentences.en: She was put in charge of handling the border by President Biden at the beginning of his administration.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，我们一直在谈论的所有这些，那种不清楚她代表什么的感觉，以及她担任副总统期间的许多竞选活动都带有这种色彩。

sentences.en: The border is now one of the biggest political liabilities that the Democrats bring into this election.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处似乎未完，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: And collectively, all that we've been talking about, the sense that it's not clear what
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处似乎未完，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: she stands for and that many of her campaigns in her tenure as vice president have been marked
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处似乎未完，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: by question marks about her, you know, effectiveness as a manager and as a leader, have added up
sentences.zh: 关于她作为管理者和领导者的能力，人们的质疑声不断累积，

sentences.en: to the electorate not having a terribly favorable impression of her at the outset of this campaign.
sentences.zh: 导致选民在竞选之初对她的印象并不怎么好。

sentences.en: Of course, what this doesn't account for is Kamala Harris's strengths, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，这并没有考虑到卡玛拉·哈里斯的优势，对吧？

sentences.en: Her searing interrogations of Brett Kavanaugh during his confirmation hearing, which thrilled liberals.
sentences.zh: 她在布雷特·卡瓦诺的确认听证会上那场尖锐的质询，让自由派大呼过瘾。

sentences.en: Her ability to speak powerfully about abortion rights and the reality that with her as a potential
sentences.zh: 她能够有力地谈论堕胎权，而现实是，如果由她作为潜在的

sentences.en: nominee, Democrats can make this race about what they always wanted it to be about, which
sentences.zh: 候选人，民主党人可以将这场竞选聚焦于他们一直想聚焦的议题，即

sentences.en: is Donald Trump rather than an aging nominee struggling to communicate from the debate stage.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普，而不是一位在辩论台上难以进行有效沟通的年迈候选人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris will have a tremendous opportunity to redefine herself to the public.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯将拥有一个绝佳的机会，向公众重新定义自己。

sentences.en: She will have many people who really want to support her.
sentences.zh: 会有很多人真心想要支持她。

sentences.en: They will be open-minded to her pitch in the weeks ahead.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，他们会以开放的心态去听取她的主张。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of Democrats are going to learn just how down in the dumps they've been over the last year when they hear someone capable of making a vigorous and energetic case
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当许多民主党人听到有人能够针对唐纳德·特朗普提出有力且充满活力的论点时，他们会意识到自己在过去一年里是多么沮丧，

sentences.en: against Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 并从中走出来。

sentences.en: That said, the reality is she enters this race as a relatively unpopular candidate who isn't the
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，现实情况是，她作为一名相对不受欢迎的候选人进入这场竞选，她并不是那个

sentences.en: broadly appealing, acceptable Democrat that the party has turned to in election after election to make contests a simple up or down referendum on Donald Trump and his allies.
sentences.zh: 党派在一次又一次选举中转而寻求的、具有广泛吸引力且易于接受的民主党人，无法让竞选变成一场针对唐纳德·特朗普及其盟友的简单信任投票。

sentences.en: And despite that, Democrat after Democrat after Democrat has come out and endorsed her candidacy,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，一位又一位民主党人还是站出来支持她的候选资格，

sentences.en: making it much harder, maybe even impossible, for there to be any serious contest for the
sentences.zh: 这使得民主党提名出现任何实质性竞争变得更加困难，甚至是不可能的。

sentences.en: Democratic nomination.
sentences.zh: 民主党提名。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，内特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: After the break, politics reporter Reed Epstein on why nobody in the Democratic Party is challenging
sentences.zh: 休息之后，政治记者里德·爱泼斯坦将分析为什么民主党内没有人挑战

sentences.en: Harris.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: When do you want to start?
sentences.zh: 你想什么时候开始？

sentences.en: As soon as humanly possible.
sentences.zh: 越快越好。

sentences.en: Oh, you there?
sentences.zh: 哦，你在吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm here.
sentences.zh: 在，我在这儿。

sentences.en: Okay, I am walking up the stairs with my headphones.
sentences.zh: 好的，我正戴着耳机走上楼梯。

sentences.en: And I'm going to plug the microphone in and how about that?
sentences.zh: 我要把麦克风插上，这样怎么样？

sentences.en: Now can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 现在你能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 听到了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Reid, we just spoke with our colleague Nate Cohn about the strength or the lack of strength of Kamala Harris's very likely Democratic nominee candidacy.
sentences.zh: 里德，我们刚才和同事内特·科恩谈到了卡玛拉·哈里斯作为极有可能的民主党提名人的实力，或者说缺乏实力的问题。

sentences.en: And his conclusion is that she's not all that strong at the moment.
sentences.zh: 他的结论是，她目前并没有那么强大。

sentences.en: Yes, she's stronger than Biden was vis-a-vis Trump, but still trails Trump in almost every poll that was done over the past year.
sentences.zh: 是的，她相对于特朗普来说比拜登更强，但在过去一年进行的几乎所有民调中，她仍然落后于特朗普。

sentences.en: So our question for you is pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 所以我们问你的问题很简单。

sentences.en: Why do you think that so many Democrats are lining up so quickly behind Kamala Harris within the past hour or so?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么这么多民主党人在过去一个小时左右的时间里迅速排队支持卡玛拉·哈里斯？

sentences.en: That now includes former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 这现在包括了前众议院议长南希·佩洛西。

sentences.en: And why is there no real challenge to her, given all that information?
sentences.zh: 鉴于所有这些信息，为什么没有对她进行真正的挑战？

sentences.en: Well, there's no challenge to her because Joe Biden made it practically impossible to challenge her.
sentences.zh: 嗯，之所以没有人挑战她，是因为乔·拜登让挑战她变得几乎不可能。

sentences.en: There was a brief window of about 20 minutes after Biden withdrew from the presidential campaign and before he endorsed Harris for someone else to run against her.
sentences.zh: 在拜登退出总统竞选到他支持哈里斯之间，有大约20分钟的短暂窗口期，可以让其他人与她竞争。

sentences.en: 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 20分钟。

sentences.en: I don't remember exactly how long it was, but it was after I saw that he had dropped out and before I got home from the pool that he had endorsed Harris.
sentences.zh: 我不记得具体有多久了，但那是在我看到他退选之后，我从游泳池回到家之前，他就已经支持哈里斯了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when he did that, he didn't just transfer political support to her.
sentences.zh: 当他这样做时，他不仅是将政治支持转移给了她。

sentences.en: He also transferred the $96 million that his campaign had in the bank, and he transferred the 1,300 people who worked for the campaign for him to her.
sentences.zh: 他还转移了竞选团队账上的9600万美元，并把为他工作的1300名竞选人员也转给了她。

sentences.en: And so for anyone to run a truncated campaign that was going to take place in just a couple of weeks targeting the 4,600 delegates to the Democratic Convention,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于任何想要进行一场仅在几周内针对民主党全国代表大会4600名代表的缩短版竞选的人来说，

sentences.en: $96 million to zero is a tough place to start.
sentences.zh: 从9600万美元对阵零美元开始，是一个非常艰难的处境。

sentences.en: And so it did make it practically impossible for anyone else to challenge Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实让其他人挑战卡玛拉·哈里斯变得几乎不可能。

sentences.en: But practically impossible doesn't mean impossible.
sentences.zh: 但几乎不可能并不意味着完全不可能。

sentences.en: So what's your understanding of why the prominent Democrats, whose names have been kicking around for a few weeks now since the debate,
sentences.zh: 那么，你对那些自辩论以来名字已经在政坛流传了几周的知名民主党人有什么了解？

sentences.en: since it occurred to many people that Biden might drop out, why have none of those names indicated any interest in challenging Harris?
sentences.zh: 自从许多人意识到拜登可能会退选以来，为什么这些人中没有一个表示出挑战哈里斯的兴趣？

sentences.en: Well, the prospect of any of these people, and we're talking about a field of white men mostly,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些人中的任何一个——我们谈论的主要是白人男性群体——

sentences.en: seeking to oust a black woman vice president who is literally next in line is politically untenable in today's Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 试图推翻一位实际上排在接班顺位第一位的黑人女性副总统，在今天的民主党内是政治上站不住脚的。

sentences.en: A party that is increasingly dependent on women and people of color,
sentences.zh: 这个党派越来越依赖女性和有色人种，

sentences.en: that the argument that any of those people that we're talking about would have needed to make really would have been built around her competence.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的那些人如果想要挑战，真正需要提出的论点必须建立在对她能力的质疑上。

sentences.en: And I don't think any of them were prepared to make that argument.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们中没有人准备好提出这样的论点。

sentences.en: You're saying that even if these potential Democratic challengers had doubts,
sentences.zh: 你是说，即使这些潜在的民主党挑战者有疑虑，

sentences.en: they would have been extremely loathe to run against Kamala Harris and be seen as trying to derail a historic nomination and in the process potentially alienating these key Democratic voting blocs that you just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 他们也会极度不愿与卡玛拉·哈里斯竞争，因为这会被视为试图破坏一个历史性的提名，并在此过程中可能疏远你刚才提到的那些关键的民主党选民群体。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These are understandable political reasons for potential rivals to sit on their hands, stay out of this race.
sentences.zh: 对于潜在的竞争对手来说，袖手旁观、不参与这场竞选是有其可理解的政治原因的。

sentences.en: They come on top of the argument that Biden just handed his entire political apparatus to Harris.
sentences.zh: 这些原因叠加在拜登刚刚将他整个政治机器移交给哈里斯这一事实之上。

sentences.en: But there is another argument for competition that I think is worth exploring, and it's the argument made as recently as 24 hours ago by Congressman Dean Phillips,
sentences.zh: 但关于竞争还有另一个论点，我认为值得探讨，这就是众议员迪恩·菲利普斯在24小时前提出的论点，

sentences.en: Democrat who challenged Biden in the primary, who says basically any competition, even if it's weak competition, does Harris favors because it forces her to become a stronger,
sentences.zh: 他在初选中挑战过拜登的民主党人，他基本上说任何竞争，即使是弱势竞争，对哈里斯都有好处，因为它迫使她成为一个更强大、

sentences.en: more battle-tested candidate in a way that she wouldn't be if she simply coronated in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 更经得起考验的候选人，如果她只是在几天内被加冕，就不会有这种效果。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that sounds right if you were writing a script for a television show, you would want there to be competition.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，如果你在写一部电视剧的剧本，你确实会希望有竞争。

sentences.en: But here in real life, Democrats are petrified of Donald Trump winning the election again,
sentences.zh: 但在现实生活中，民主党人对唐纳德·特朗普再次赢得选举感到恐惧，

sentences.en: and they are eager to move forward with a candidate who they can unite behind and make the case that Donald Trump should not be elected.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望推进一位能够团结一致支持的候选人，并提出唐纳德·特朗普不应被选出的理由。

sentences.en: And the problem with Biden over the last three and a half weeks, most acutely, but more broadly since the beginning of his campaign,
sentences.zh: 而拜登在过去三周半里，最严重的问题，或者说从他竞选开始以来更广泛的问题，

sentences.en: was that Democrats and the Biden campaign could not convince voters that Biden was up to the job of being the president again for another four years.
sentences.zh: 在于民主党人和拜登竞选团队无法说服选民，拜登有能力再担任四年总统。

sentences.en: And if you couldn't get voters to buy into that, you couldn't get to the second point, which was that Donald Trump is a threat to X, Y, and Z.
sentences.zh: 如果你不能让选民接受这一点，你就无法进入第二点，即唐纳德·特朗普对某某某构成了威胁。

sentences.en: And so that was really the problem with Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是拜登的问题所在。

sentences.en: And they think that Harris is going to be able to prosecute the case of all the things that they want voters to worry about with Trump in a way that Biden could not.
sentences.zh: 他们认为哈里斯将能够以拜登无法做到的方式，就选民关心的所有关于特朗普的问题进行辩论。

sentences.en: And the first order of business on that is abortion, an issue in which she is far more comfortable talking about than Biden is, and a much,
sentences.zh: 而这方面的首要任务是堕胎，这是一个她比拜登谈论起来舒服得多的议题，而且她是一个比拜登更出色、

sentences.en: far more adept messenger to make the case about Trump and abortion rights than Biden ever has been.
sentences.zh: 更娴熟的传达者，能够就特朗普和堕胎权问题进行辩论。

sentences.en: So that's an area where you're looking for early signs that Kamala Harris, the likely nominee,
sentences.zh: 所以，你正在寻找早期迹象，看看卡玛拉·哈里斯这位可能的提名人，

sentences.en: is truly able to distinguish herself and prove herself perhaps a possessor of greater political skills than she is by reputation.
sentences.zh: 是否真的能够脱颖而出，证明自己可能拥有比外界评价更高的政治技巧。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think her political skills are better than her reputation, frankly.
sentences.zh: 是的，坦率地说，我认为她的政治技巧比她的名声要好。

sentences.en: She ran a lousy campaign for president in 2020.
sentences.zh: 她在2020年竞选总统时表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And then after Joe Biden was elected, she was handed a portfolio of impossible issues.
sentences.zh: 而在乔·拜登当选后，她被分配了一系列不可能完成的任务。

sentences.en: She was given the border.
sentences.zh: 她被分配处理边境问题。

sentences.en: She was given voting rights.
sentences.zh: 她被分配处理投票权问题。

sentences.en: But really, since the Dobbs decision two years ago, she's been a much more capable public performer.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，自两年前多布斯案裁决以来，她作为公众人物的表现要出色得多。

sentences.en: And my guess is that people who, for whom the image of her was cemented early in her vice presidency,
sentences.zh: 我猜，那些在副总统任期早期就对她形成刻板印象的人，

sentences.en: may wind up being surprised at how she performs under the bright lights of being the nominee herself.
sentences.zh: 最终可能会对她在作为提名人亲自站在聚光灯下的表现感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We talked about this with Nate.
sentences.zh: 我们和内特谈过这个。

sentences.en: It's extremely possible that Kamala Harris will be a successful Democratic nominee.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯极有可能成为一位成功的民主党提名人。

sentences.en: She's already clearly energized many Democrats who were totally crestfallen over what happened with Biden.
sentences.zh: 她显然已经激励了许多对拜登发生的事情感到沮丧的民主党人。

sentences.en: But if it turns out that her short general election campaign doesn't go well, and if she doesn't beat Trump,
sentences.zh: 但如果事实证明她短暂的大选竞选并不顺利，如果她没能击败特朗普，

sentences.en: how much of the blame will belong directly to Joe Biden for putting the party and Harris in this situation by discouraging anyone else from running against him,
sentences.zh: 那么乔·拜登要承担多少直接责任？因为他通过阻止任何人与他竞争，将党派和哈里斯置于这种境地，

sentences.en: by snuffing out any whiff of competition?
sentences.zh: 通过扼杀任何竞争的苗头？

sentences.en: I mean, he changed the primary calendar to favor him and him alone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他改变了初选日程，只对他自己有利。

sentences.en: He ditched Iowa and started the primaries in South Carolina, a state he knew he would win.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了爱荷华州，在南卡罗来纳州开始了初选，这是一个他知道自己会赢的州。

sentences.en: I mean, how much of this is going to be on him if Harris loses?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果哈里斯输了，这其中有多少责任要归咎于他？

sentences.en: Well, you should be clear that Biden made a choice to seek reelection, but it was the rest of the party, with the exception of a little-known congressman from Minnesota,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你应该清楚，拜登做出了寻求连任的选择，但除了来自明尼苏达州的一位鲜为人知的众议员外，是党内其他人，

sentences.en: who made the collective decision not to challenge Joe Biden for reelection.
sentences.zh: 做出了集体决定，不去挑战乔·拜登的连任。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: I remember having conversations with people before Biden formally entered the race that there would have been tens of millions of dollars available for a candidate in the mold of Bernie Sanders to run from Biden's left.
sentences.zh: 我记得在拜登正式进入竞选之前，曾与人交谈过，当时有数千万美元可供像伯尼·桑德斯那样的人从拜登的左翼进行竞选。

sentences.en: There was talk of billionaire candidates like J.B.
sentences.zh: 当时有传言说像J.B.普利兹克这样的亿万富翁候选人会加入竞选并自筹资金，但我认为把缺乏竞争的责任完全归咎于拜登并不公平。

sentences.en: Pritzker getting in the race and self-funding, but I don't think it's necessarily fair to blame Biden for the lack of competition.
sentences.zh: 是党内其他人掩耳盗铃，告诉所有人拜登没问题，他们在这方面承担了更多的责任。

sentences.en: It's the rest of the party that covered their eyes and told everyone that Biden would be fine that bear more of the responsibility on this front.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到好奇，作为最后一个问题，

sentences.en: And that makes me wonder, as a concluding question here,
sentences.zh: 你认为民主党是否需要就竞争以及更多人参与这些竞选进行更广泛的讨论？

sentences.en: do you think that the Democratic Party needs to just have a bigger conversation about competition and about more people entering into these races?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尽管唐纳德·特朗普在共和党内影响巨大，但共和党方面并不缺乏竞争。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no absence of competition on the Republican side, despite the huge way in which Donald Trump looms over that party.
sentences.zh: 今年有几位州长与他竞争，尽管他有明显的优势。

sentences.en: You had multiple governors running against him this year, despite his obvious strengths.
sentences.zh: 而民主党方面却什么都没有。

sentences.en: And nothing on the Democratic side.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论结果如何，这是否是你期望民主党开始讨论的话题？

sentences.en: And so is that a conversation you expect the Democrats to start having, really, no matter how this turns out?
sentences.zh: 你知道，迈克尔，这与其说是一个关于竞争的故事，不如说是一个关于党内精英不听取选民意见的故事。

sentences.en: You know, Michael, this is less a story about competition as it is a story about the elites of the party not listening to their own voters.
sentences.zh: 多年来有充分的证据表明，很大比例的民主党人并不希望乔·拜登竞选第二个任期。

sentences.en: There was ample evidence over years that large percentages of Democrats did not want Joe Biden to run for a second term.
sentences.zh: 但当他这样做时，他们都退到一边，给了他一条通往提名的平坦道路。

sentences.en: But when he did, they all stepped aside and gave him a glide path to the nomination anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们得到的结果是一位有严重缺陷的候选人，无法坚持到终点线。

sentences.en: And the result that they got was a deeply flawed nominee who couldn't make it to the finish line.
sentences.zh: 现在竞选已经到了后期，没有时间进行真正的竞争来取代他了。

sentences.en: And now it's so late in the game that there's no time to have a real competition to replace him.
sentences.zh: 里德，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Reeves, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 周一晚上，大多数民主党代表支持哈里斯副总统作为拜登的继任者，

sentences.en: On Monday night, a majority of Democratic delegates endorsed Vice President Harris as Biden's replacement,
sentences.zh: 她迅速采取行动，确立了自己作为事实上的民主党提名人的地位。

sentences.en: and she moved quickly to assert herself as the de facto Democratic nominee.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯要求前司法部长埃里克·霍尔德监督她选择竞选搭档的过程，

sentences.en: Harris asked former Attorney General Eric Holder to oversee her choice of a running mate
sentences.zh: 并说服拜登竞选团队的现任领导层留任，继续为她对阵特朗普的竞选工作服务。

sentences.en: and persuaded the current leadership of Biden's campaign to remain in place and run her campaign against Trump.
sentences.zh: 在这场竞选中，我将自豪地，我将自豪地把我的记录与他的进行对比。

sentences.en: And in this campaign, I will proudly, I will proudly put my record against his.
sentences.zh: 最后，在她的第一次竞选演讲中，哈里斯直接向特朗普发起了挑战，提到了她作为律师和检察官的经历。

sentences.en: Finally, in her first campaign speech, Harris took Trump on directly, invoking her history as a lawyer and a prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 在这些角色中，我打击了各种各样的犯罪者。

sentences.en: In those roles, I took on perpetrators of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 虐待女性的掠夺者。

sentences.en: Predators who abused women.
sentences.zh: 欺骗消费者的诈骗犯。

sentences.en: Fraudsters who ripped off consumers.
sentences.zh: 为了私利破坏规则的骗子。

sentences.en: Cheaters who broke the rules for their own gain.
sentences.zh: 所以请听我说，我了解唐纳德·特朗普这类人。

sentences.en: So hear me when I say, I know Donald Trump's type.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 特勤局的神圣使命是保护我们国家的领导人。

sentences.en: The Secret Service's solemn mission is to protect our nation's leaders.
sentences.zh: 7月13日，我们失败了。

sentences.en: On July 13th, we failed.
sentences.zh: 周一在一次激烈的国会听证会上，特勤局局长金伯利·切特尔

sentences.en: During a heated congressional hearing on Monday, Secret Service Director Kimberly Cheadle
sentences.zh: 面对关于她所在机构在唐纳德·特朗普被枪击当天保护计划的愤怒质询。

sentences.en: faced angry questions about her agency's plan to protect Donald Trump on the day when he was shot.
sentences.zh: 但她多次拒绝回答关于他安保工作的基本询问。

sentences.en: But she repeatedly declined to answer basic inquiries about his security.
sentences.zh: 你真的相信这个国家的大多数人现在对你有信心吗？

sentences.en: Do you really believe that the majority of this country has confidence in you right now?
sentences.zh: 结果，两党的议员都告诉切特尔，她已经失去了他们的信任。

sentences.en: As a result, lawmakers from both parties told Cheadle that she had lost their confidence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听着，切特尔局长，我认为你应该辞职。

sentences.en: Well, look, I believe, Director Cheadle, that you should resign.
sentences.zh: 我想两党都有同事持这种看法，我希望你能考虑一下。

sentences.en: I think there are colleagues on both sides of the aisle who believe that, and I hope you'll consider it.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能考虑一下。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种喝断片儿才睡着的人。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
